# PRISM — Pakistan Climate Intelligence

PRISM is an independent evidence-first monitoring pilot, not an official warning service.

## Scientific integrity
- Never interpret missing measurements as zero or safety.
- Forecasts and modelled air/discharge are not physical gauge observations.
- Coverage: 12 national-comparison reference coordinates; 160 dated district records are available separately.
- Flood risk remains UNASSESSED. No calibrated inundation, return periods or GLOF predictions.
- Seven-section officer responses are deterministic evidence briefs. Optional browser-local WebLLM selects existing facts; hosted LLM tool calling is not configured.
- NASA GIBS map layers and nearest visualization-pixel classification are supported, with cloud/no-data ambiguity. These are not validated inundation or ground confirmation.
- RainViewer exposes past radar metadata, not guaranteed Pakistan coverage or future nowcast.

## Machine interfaces
GET /api/public/v1/locations
GET /api/public/v1/districts/:slug
GET /api/public/v1/point?lat=24.8607&lon=67.0011
GET /api/public/v1/sources
GET /api/public/v1/briefings?kind=family&location=karachi
POST /api/officer
POST /mcp — JSON-RPC initialize, tools/list, tools/call

An envelope retains source identity, documentation URL, evidence tier, model family, latency, retrieval timestamp and source valid timestamp. Failure data is null; error code and reason are explicit. Source health is isolate-local rather than globally durable.

## District expansion and archives
160 dated OCHA/WFP COD-AB v01 district records (valid 2022-09-09, reviewed 2024-09-27); 162 unique named routes preserve Karachi/Chitral city references. National comparison remains 12 city samples. /api/public/v1/district-registry contains source and PCodes. /api/public/v1/gdacs provides country-attributed source reports. /api/public/v1/chirps?location=karachi polls ClimateSERV and shows a publication-lag-aware archive; partial totals remain null. Neither source establishes absence of hazard.

## Detailed forecast (0.4)
GET /api/public/v1/weather-detail?location=karachi: provenance envelope with 168 future hourly slots, seven rolling 24-hour windows, apparent temperature, humidity, wind/gusts and precipitation probability. Null values are retained; incomplete aggregates are null. Same numerical-weather-models family as core weather, never an extra independent consensus vote. /forecast includes accessible charts, hourly text table, CSV/JSON export and print report. MCP weather_detail exposes the same contract. GET /openapi.json provides the principal public API specification.

GET /api/public/v1/readiness checks the four core Karachi point feeds. HTTP 503 means degraded; HTTP 200 is scoped feed availability, not hazard safety or production certification. GET /api/public/v1/health checks application reachability.

## Real date and freshness (0.4.1)
GET /api/public/v1/time returns uncached server UTC time with the Asia/Karachi display timezone. Browser clocks are anchored to server time and a monotonic timer. Forecast caches expire at UTC hour boundaries, including midnight; source badges distinguish forecasts, archives, static data, stale observations and unverified timestamps. Archive data is never relabelled as today. Daily publication rejects future or old generation/retrieval times.

## Community context (0.5.0)
NASA FIRMS uses the public South Asia VIIRS SNPP CSV filtered to the monitoring rectangle; provider observation timestamps can lag. No key is required for that download. ReliefWeb now targets v2 and still requires approved RELIEFWEB_APPNAME. OpenAQ requires OPENAQ_KEY.
Population, infrastructure and community-context public v1 endpoints accept a registered location. Population is a WorldPop 2025 model estimate for a query square, not a district census or exposed population. OSM facilities retain source identity and database timestamp; names may be missing and operational status is unverified. The Officer consults these sources for population/facility questions.
